716183_6cba412c.text: Orexin A and orexin B (also known as hypocretin 1 and hypocretin 2) are neuropeptides that are expressed in a population of neurons in the lateral hypothalamic area (LHA) (Lecea et al., 1998)(Sakurai et al., 1998). Disruption of this neuropeptide system causes narcolepsy in human and animals, suggesting that orexins are crucial regulators of sleep and wakefulness (Sakurai, 2007). Orexin-producing neurons (orexin neurons) send axonal projections widely in CNS regions that regulate emotion, sleep, wakefulness, arousal, the reward system and energy homeostasis (Sakurai et al., 2011). Especially dense projections of orexin neurons are found in the monoaminergic and cholinergic nuclei in the hypothalamus and brainstem (Nambu et al., 1999)(Horvath et al., 1999)(Brown et al., 2001)(Eggermann et al., 2001)(Yamanaka et al., 2002)(Peyron et al., 1998). Orexin neurons regulate cholinergic/monoaminergic neurons to maintain a long, consolidated waking period. Orexin neurons receive abundant input from the limbic system, preoptic area, posterior hypothalamus and brain stem [16]17]
